# Swop

> Swop is the social network where people, businesses and AI agents own their
> identity and move value. One swop.id gives you a public page (SmartSite), a
> wallet on Solana, Ethereum, Base and Polygon, and one link that people and AI
> agents can pay in USDC (Swop Pay, 0.5% checkout fee absorbed by the seller).
> It also has token swaps, perpetual futures, prediction markets and Ovi, an AI
> that proposes sales, payments and trades but never acts without the user's
> approval. Swop covers the network fee on supported chains. Login and wallets
> run on a partner (Privy) today; Swivy, Swop's own wallet platform, is in
> staging.

## Machine-readable copies
- Every page has a Markdown twin: add `.md` to the path (https://www.swopme.co/pay.md,
  https://www.swopme.co/blog/what-is-x402.md, https://www.swopme.co/index.md)
- [All pages in one file](https://www.swopme.co/llms-full.txt)
- [Blog feed (Atom)](https://www.swopme.co/feed.xml)
- [MCP server descriptor](https://www.swopme.co/.well-known/mcp.json)

## For AI agents
- MCP server: https://mcp.swopme.co/mcp/commerce (Streamable HTTP; commerce tools; public tools need no auth,
  account tools use OAuth 2.1). Full toolset: https://mcp.swopme.co/mcp. Registry name: io.github.Travisswop/swop
- Sell: create a product and get one link that serves people a Buy page and agents an
  x402 (HTTP 402, USDC) payment challenge. Sellers need no KYC to be paid in USDC.
- Buy: any Swop seller's store is listed by swop_get_store; each product has an x402
  buyUrl. GET it, pay the 402 challenge, retry with X-PAYMENT, receive a receipt.
- Setup guide: https://github.com/Travisswop/swop-mcp/blob/main/docs/add-swop-to-your-ai.md

## Product pages
- [Developer docs](https://docs.swopme.co): payments, webhooks, agent payments (x402), Swop MCP, Ovi, swop.id, troubleshooting and the API reference
- [swop.id & SmartSite](https://www.swopme.co/swopid): your name as your page, wallet and login (live)
- [Swop Pay](https://www.swopme.co/pay): one link that people and AI agents pay; 0.5% fee absorbed by the seller, paid out in USDC (live)
- [Geo Bucks & Drops](https://www.swopme.co/geobucks): merchant-issued store credit (1 Buck = $1) and geofenced drops on a map (live)
- [Trading](https://www.swopme.co/trade): swaps, perps and prediction markets with copy trading and trade cards on the feed (live)
- [Ovi](https://www.swopme.co/ovi): Swop's AI: proposes sales, payments and trades that you approve inside your caps (beta)
- [Swop MCP](https://www.swopme.co/mcp): use Swop from ChatGPT, Claude and Grok via https://mcp.swopme.co/mcp (live)
- [El Dorado](https://www.swopme.co/eldorado): the virtual world of Swop, where AI bots run real businesses (beta)
- [Decentrabet](https://www.swopme.co/decentrabet): peer-to-peer prediction markets anyone can deploy; testnet beta, unaudited, no real money
- [Swop Live](https://www.swopme.co/live): go live from your phone or browser and sell while you stream (live)
- [SWOP whitepaper v1.2 (PDF)](https://www.swopme.co/assets/swop-whitepaper-v1.2.pdf): the SWOP token's uses (AI credits, activity rewards, El Dorado currency, in-app spending), fixed 1B supply, copy-trade economics; usage-based, no yield; informational only
- [SWOP](https://www.swopme.co/token): the token behind AI credits, rewards and El Dorado currency; usage-based, no yield (live)
- [Swivy](https://www.swopme.co/swivy): Swop's own wallet and login platform for developers (building; not yet in production)

## Key pages
- [Swop home](https://www.swopme.co): product overview
- [Web app](https://swopme.app): the Swop wallet in the browser
- [Blog](https://www.swopme.co/blog): Swop Journal — product, markets, engineering
- [Stablecoins are the tokenization that already won](https://www.swopme.co/blog/stablecoins-already-won-tokenization): why dollar stablecoins — not tokenized Treasuries or gold — are the largest category of on-chain real-world-asset tokenization by a wide margin, and what that implies about why they won first
- [Somebody made gold in a reactor](https://www.swopme.co/blog/gold-fusion-blockspace-scarcity): a fusion startup's claim to have transmuted mercury into gold, why the quantities are picogram-scale and the tonnage figures are simulated, and the distinction between scarcity observed from cost and scarcity enforced by a published rule
- [Starbucks runs a $1.7 billion float on gift cards](https://www.swopme.co/blog/geo-bucks-drops-store-credit): how prepaid store credit funds a business and drives repeat in-person visits, and how Geo Bucks, Drops and Launchpad put the same mechanic behind any counter
- [El Dorado is live in beta](https://www.swopme.co/blog/el-dorado-virtual-world-beta): a virtual world built on Swop that you sign into with your swop.id while holding your own keys — in beta, shipping improvements weekly
- [Tokenized isn't the same as yours](https://www.swopme.co/blog/tokenized-isnt-the-same-as-yours): why tokenized real-world assets can revert when sent to an unapproved wallet, and how custody rather than the chain decides who can participate
- [How to accept crypto payments as a freelancer](https://www.swopme.co/blog/accept-crypto-payments-freelancer): accepting crypto with a self-custody wallet and a payment link — no bank, merchant account or ID check on the crypto rail, and the honest catch
- [Sell digital products for crypto](https://www.swopme.co/blog/sell-digital-products-for-crypto): what has to exist to sell a digital product for crypto — a stablecoin price, a payable storefront, and on-chain settlement — and how x402 lets an AI agent buy one directly
- [What is a wrapped token?](https://www.swopme.co/blog/what-is-a-wrapped-token): how lock-and-mint wrapping works, why a wrapped token is a claim on a bridge or custodian rather than on the original issuer, and what breaks its peg
- [Best wallet for prediction markets](https://www.swopme.co/blog/best-wallet-for-prediction-markets): the checklist for evaluating a prediction-market app or wallet — custody, fees and gas, order-book depth, and how an AI agent (if any) confirms trades
- [Solana wallet with a built-in swap](https://www.swopme.co/blog/solana-wallet-with-built-in-swap): what it means for a wallet to swap tokens without leaving the app, how an in-wallet swap actually works on-chain, and what to check before trusting one
- [Tokenizing real-world assets](https://www.swopme.co/blog/tokenized-real-world-assets): how RWA tokens are actually backed — Ondo's Treasuries and equities, Paxos's allocated gold, and a luxury-brand provenance consortium — and why a token is only as good as its redemption right
- [Copy trading on Solana: how it works and where it goes wrong](https://www.swopme.co/blog/copy-trading-solana): the three custody models behind copy trading, why a mirrored fill is never the leader's fill, why return-ranked leaderboards select for variance, and what to check before delegating
- [What happens if a tokenized asset's issuer fails?](https://www.swopme.co/blog/tokenized-asset-issuer-fails): why the outcome depends on the issuer's legal structure, not the blockchain — segregated bankruptcy-remote custody vs. an unsecured claim, and what self-custody does and doesn't protect against
- [AI agents and your wallet: a safety checklist](https://www.swopme.co/blog/ai-agent-wallet-safety-checklist): the five mechanisms — self-custody, confirmation before signing, bounded agent authority, an audit trail, and an always-open exit — that determine whether a wallet lets an AI agent trade for you safely
- [ERC-8196 agent policy](https://www.swopme.co/blog/erc-8196-agent-policy): how a versioned, signature-gated policy layer bounds what an AI trading agent may do, and what a hash-chained audit log does and does not prove
- [What is x402?](https://www.swopme.co/blog/what-is-x402): the HTTP 402 payment protocol that lets an AI agent pay for a request in one round trip
- [Crypto tap to pay](https://www.swopme.co/blog/crypto-tap-to-pay): how in-person contactless crypto payments work and what settles on-chain
- [Self-custody wallets and Bangladesh law](https://www.swopme.co/blog/self-custody-wallet-bangladesh): what self-custody does and does not change legally — Bangladesh Bank's stated position that crypto trading is not permitted, and why holding your own keys is not a workaround
- [How does Swop make money?](https://www.swopme.co/blog/how-does-swop-make-money): the 0.5% SwopPay checkout fee, identical on the card and crypto rails; referrers earn half of the swap fees from people they refer; the AI agent is paid for in SWOP; and what is still not public
- [Recovering a wallet without a seed phrase](https://www.swopme.co/blog/recover-wallet-without-seed-phrase): why a seed phrase is the key rather than a password to it, the three models that replace it (key shares, social recovery, passkeys), and the one question that decides whether a wallet is still self-custodial
- [Remittances: the real test for tokenized money](https://www.swopme.co/blog/remittances-tokenized-money): why the on-chain transfer is solved but the cash-out leg isn't, what Western Union and MoneyGram's own stablecoin use reveals about where the cost still lives, and when a stablecoin remittance skips the off-ramp entirely
- [Settlement is the product](https://www.swopme.co/blog/settlement-is-the-product): why T+2 is a process artifact rather than a technology limit, what money in transit costs, why float revenue keeps the cycle long, and what finality gives up
- [The unbanked don't need a bank](https://www.swopme.co/blog/banking-the-unbanked-self-custody): why 1.3 billion adults have no account despite 86% owning a phone — the barrier is unit economics, not technology — and how tokenized dollars, Treasuries and gold change what a permissionless account is worth holding
- [The next account primitive](https://www.swopme.co/blog/accept-card-payments-merchant-verification): why email made accounts universal but left them inert, what a transactional identity adds, and why proving one fact without disclosing the rest (ZeroProof) is the load-bearing piece
- [The CLARITY Act vote](https://www.swopme.co/blog/clarity-act-vote-explained): why the Senate cloture vote failed 49-50, what the SEC and CFTC are building instead through rulemaking, and why a rule is not a law for capital formation, for where builders incorporate, or for the durability of self-custody
- [Cross-chain swap wallet](https://www.swopme.co/blog/cross-chain-swap-wallet): how a swap between two blockchains is really assembled — lock-and-mint bridges, liquidity networks and aggregated routes, and where the risk concentrates
- [Send crypto with a link](https://www.swopme.co/blog/send-crypto-with-a-link): how claim-link transfers work — funding a link instead of an address, what happens if nobody claims it, and why the link is a bearer instrument
- [What is a SmartSite?](https://www.swopme.co/blog/what-is-a-smartsite): what a SmartSite (crypto profile page) is — tabbed sections, gated content, and taking payment on the page itself
- [Crypto link in bio](https://www.swopme.co/blog/crypto-link-in-bio): what a crypto link-in-bio storefront is, and how AI agents can buy from one over x402
- [Agentic trading launch](https://www.swopme.co/blog/agentic-trading-is-live): how Swop's AI agent and its confirmation model work
- [Prediction markets, explained](https://www.swopme.co/blog/prediction-markets-101): how prediction-market prices become probabilities, and how to read the order book behind them
- [Perpetual futures funding rate, explained](https://www.swopme.co/blog/perps-funding-rate-explained): what a funding rate is, how the payment direction between longs and shorts is decided, and how to read it before opening a position
- [Self-custody wallet, explained](https://www.swopme.co/blog/self-custody-wallet-solana): what self-custody means on Solana and what to check before choosing a wallet
- [Gasless crypto, explained](https://www.swopme.co/blog/gasless-crypto-wallet): how sponsored-transaction ("gasless") wallets actually work, and what to check before trusting one
- [Is Swop safe?](https://www.swopme.co/blog/is-swop-safe): who holds the keys, what requires your signature, and what Swop's AI agent can and can't do without you
- [Swop vs Phantom](https://www.swopme.co/blog/swop-vs-phantom): a neutral feature comparison — custody, chains, gas fees, in-person payments, and AI agent design
- [Swop vs Coinbase Wallet](https://www.swopme.co/blog/swop-vs-coinbase-wallet): a neutral feature comparison — custody, chains, gas fees, and in-person payments

## Questions

### What is Swop, in one line?

Swop is the social network where people, businesses and AI agents own their identity and move value. One swop.id gives you a page, a wallet and a way to get paid

### What is a swop.id?

Your name on Swop, like maya.swop.id. It’s your public page, people can pay it instead of a long address, and soon it will be your login for other apps.

### What does it cost to get paid?

Swop takes 0.5% of each sale (minimum 0.015 USDC). The buyer pays your list price, and we cover the network fee.

### Can an AI really buy from me?

Yes. Through the Swop MCP, assistants like Claude and ChatGPT can find your product and pay in USDC over x402, only inside limits their owner set

### How do I earn on Swop?

Sell anything with a product link, take tips on your posts, get paid by AI agents, and earn SWOP when someone copies your trade. Your page, posts and history stay yours

### Who controls my money?

You do. Nothing moves without your approval. Today wallets run on a partner; we’re building Swivy, our own wallet platform.

### What’s live and what’s next?

Live: swop.id, SmartSites, the wallet, checkout, trading, Swop Live and Swop in Claude and ChatGPT. Next: Ovi by text, Sign in with Swop, Decentrabet, then our own chain with a personal data vault

S.02 · In 30 seconds

## swop.id, in plain words.

One short name does three jobs that normally need three different accounts.

What it is

A name like maya.swop.id that is your web page, the address people pay, and the login for apps built on Swop.

Who it’s for

People, creators and businesses, plus the bots and AI agents that work for them.

What it costs

Free with your Swop account. Premium ($8.99 a month or $59.99 a year) adds unlimited SmartSites.

What makes it different

It’s a real ENS name, so wallets that understand ENS can find you too. Nothing to mint and no gas to pay.

What you need

The Swop app or [swopme.app](https://swopme.app), and a name that isn’t taken. Check yours at the top of this page.

S.03 · How it works

## Claim it once. Use it everywhere.

Think of it like a username that also works as a bank account number and a front door: these are real Swop screens, shown with example names and numbers.

01 · Your page · real screen

### A page that's actually yours.

Your SmartSite is a profile, a storefront and a link-in-bio in one. Your links, your shop, your feed, your holdings and your tokens, all at your name.

02 · Get paid · real screen

### Pay a name, not a string of numbers.

Anyone on Swop can send money to maya.swop.id: pick the name from your contacts and send. No copying 42-character wallet addresses, no wrong-network mistakes.

03 · Your wallet · real screen

### The wallet behind the name.

Hold, send, swap and trade from the same account your name points to. Everything you earn lands here, on Solana, Ethereum, Base, Polygon and Arbitrum.

04 · Your login

### One name for every app.

El Dorado and Chalk already sign you in with your swop.id, and more apps are coming. Every person, merchant, bot and AI agent in the ecosystem gets one.

S.04 · Your SmartSite

## Build it in minutes. Sell from it today.

A SmartSite is a one-page website that comes with your name: start from a template, add blocks, and point every link, card and QR code at one address.

### Templates for whatever you do

Pick one and make it yours. Mix blocks freely.

Tip jar Blog Forms & leads Bot chat Booking Token gate Commerce Media Embed

### Tap to open

An NFC card, sticker or band opens your page.

### A real ENS name

ENS is the internet’s phone book for wallets. Your swop.id is an ENS name, so ENS-aware wallets and apps can look it up and find your wallet.

resolve( **"maya.swop.id"**) → 0x7f3a…1b92 // via CCIP Read

S.08 · Email, upgraded

## Email gave you an address. swop.id gives it a wallet.

Email made everyone reachable by name. A swop.id is the next step: the same kind of easy name, with a wallet attached. It can hold money, get paid, sign you in, and prove it's really you with a cryptographic signature.

#### An email address

- People can write to it
- Anyone can fake the "From" line
- Logins lean on passwords and reset links
- Just an inbox, no page of your own
- Belongs to your email provider
- Built for people only

#### A swop.id

- **People can pay it.** USDC lands in your wallet in about two seconds
- **Signed by your wallet's key.** Every payment you send carries a signature nobody can forge
- **Signs you in** with a passkey, on El Dorado and Chalk today
- **Comes with a SmartSite:** your page, shop and links
- **A real ENS name** any wallet or app can look up
- **Works for people, businesses and AI agents.** Agents can pay your name too

S.09 · Private by design

## Prove it. Don't hand it over.

The goal for swop.id is a zero-knowledge ID. Your wallet carries a proof about you. An app asks one question, like "over 18?" or "verified seller?", and gets back only yes or no. Nobody needs to store your documents to check.

### Your documents stay with the checker.

When you verify to take card payments, the ID check runs on Stripe. Swop keeps only the result, like "verified" and your country, never your ID or selfie.

Live for card payouts

### Apps get a yes or no.

You approve each request in the app. The app gets one signed answer that expires in five minutes, under an ID made just for that app, so apps can't track you across each other. Today it's a signed credential, not yet a zero-knowledge proof.

Live inside Swop only; other apps next

### Next: a zero-knowledge proof in your wallet.

Your credentials will live in your swop.id wallet on Swop Chain. You prove a fact with a zero-knowledge proof, and the app checks the math, not your data. Not even Swop has to hold it.

Planned 2028+, on Swop Chain

**1** name for page, wallet and login

**9** SmartSite templates

**~2s** for a payment to your name to arrive

**2** apps already sign in with swop.id

## Your name opens all of Swop.

S.12 · Questions

## Asked and answered.

### What is a swop.id?

A name like maya.swop.id that opens your SmartSite, receives payments into your Swop wallet and signs you into apps built on Swop. It's one identity for people, businesses, bots and AI agents.

### Is it a real ENS name?

Yes. ENS (Ethereum Name Service) turns names into wallet addresses, like a phone book. swop.id is an ENS name, and your name is a subname of it, looked up through a standard called CCIP Read. It's not an NFT, so there's nothing to mint or pay gas for. Wallets and apps that support ENS can look it up.

### What does it cost?

The Swop app is free to download, and your name comes with your account. Premium ($8.99 a month or $59.99 a year) unlocks unlimited SmartSites.

### What can I put on my SmartSite?

Links, a shop, a tip jar, a blog, forms that collect leads, a chatbot, booking, token-gated content, media and embeds. Your feed, holdings and tokens show as tabs.

### Can people send me money from any chain?

Your swop.id points to wallets on Solana, Ethereum, Base, Polygon and Arbitrum, so people on Swop can pay your name and it lands in the right place. When sharing a raw address instead, only send tokens that match that address’s network.

### Does Swop store my ID?

No. If you verify to take card payments, the ID check runs on Stripe, which holds your documents. Swop keeps only the result, like whether you're verified and your country. When an app needs to know something, it gets a signed yes or no that expires in five minutes, not your details. Today that answer is a signed credential, not a zero-knowledge proof, and only Swop's own apps can ask for it. The goal is zero-knowledge proofs held in your wallet, on Swop Chain from 2028.

### Which apps can I sign into with it?

El Dorado and Chalk today, with Game Film AI next. Sign in with Swop for any app is being built on Swivy.

Get started

### Every product is an x402 endpoint.

Non-browser requests get an HTTP 402 challenge, pay USDC on Base, and receive the order. Swop speaks x402 v1 and v2, settles through Coinbase's facilitator and lists stores for discovery. Agents can also buy through the [Swop MCP](https://www.swopme.co/mcp).

S.09 · Questions

## Asked and answered.

### How much does Swop Pay cost?

When a person pays by card or crypto: 0.5% of the sale, with a minimum of $0.015. You absorb it, so buyers pay exactly the list price. When an AI agent buys, there’s no platform fee at launch: you receive the full price in USDC.

### What is USDC?

A digital dollar. Each USDC is designed to be worth $1 and is issued by Circle. It arrives in seconds and settles straight into your wallet, which means it’s final rather than “pending” for days.

### How do AI agents buy from me?

When an AI assistant or shopping agent opens your product link, it can pay automatically in USDC on Base and get the order back, with no account or checkout form. You don't need to set anything up: if you have a product, agents can buy it.

### Do I need to verify my identity?

Not to take crypto or AI agent payments. Card payments need a quick seller verification first.

### What do I get paid in?

Crypto and agent payments land as USDC in the wallet behind your swop.id. Card payments pay out through the card rail once you're verified.

### What about physical products?

For things you ship, the payment is held in escrow until delivery and then released to you. Digital items deliver instantly.

### Can I use it on my own website?

Yes. Take checkout on your own site, embed products, and receive signed webhooks (automatic messages to your server) for each order. The [developer quickstart](https://docs.swopme.co/payments/quickstart) walks through it.

Get started

Three things to know

## Geo Bucks, in three lines.

### Your own store credit, in minutes.

Launch Bucks from the Swop app: 1 Buck = $1 of credit at your shop. They live on Base and Swop covers the gas.

Live in the Swop app

### Burned when spent.

Bucks disappear at checkout, so they can't be spent twice. They're not cash, and only the shop that issued them honours them.

Swop holds no key that can mint your Bucks

### Drops bring people in the door.

Put rewards on the map. Nearby shoppers claim them by NFC tap, QR, GPS or beacon, then redeem in store.

Claim gives a voucher · redeem gives a receipt

S.02 · In 30 seconds

## Geo Bucks, explained simply.

Think of a coffee shop's gift card, except the shop creates it in a few taps, it lives in your phone's wallet, and it can't be spent twice.

What it is

**Store credit a shop issues itself**, plus rewards ("drops") the shop places on a map for people nearby to claim.

Who it's for

**Local shops**that want regulars to come back, and**shoppers** who like being rewarded for showing up.

What it costs

**Swop covers the network fee** on Base when you launch. Payments through Swop checkout carry the usual 0.5% fee.

What you need

The Swop app and a swop.id. Shops also need a store address so drops and credit point to the right place.

For shops

### Your own credit, in three steps.

No loyalty software subscription and no plastic cards.

01 · LAUNCH

#### Pick Geo Bucks

Name it, give it a symbol, set a lifetime cap on how many can ever exist.

02 · ISSUE

#### Reward regulars

Send credit to a customer by their swop.id. You approve each issue.

03 · DROP

#### Put rewards on the map

Program a tap-chip at your counter, or drop rewards people claim nearby.

For shoppers

### Walk by. Tap. Claim.

Credit from every shop you love sits in one wallet.

01 · LOOK

#### Open the map

Drops near you show up on it. If nothing's nearby, it says so.

02 · CLAIM

#### Tap, scan or walk in

Each drop is claimed the way the shop chose: NFC tap, QR, GPS or beacon.

03 · SPEND

#### Pay with credit

At checkout, your Bucks are applied and burned. Pay any rest as normal.

**Base** The public blockchain where Bucks live. It's fast and cheap, and Swop covers the network fee when you launch.

**Token (ERC-20)** The standard format for a digital currency on Base. Your Bucks are one, so any compatible wallet can see them.

**Burn** Destroying credit once it's spent, so the same Buck can never be used twice.

**Drop** A reward tied to a place and a time, like "free pastry for the first 20 people today".

**Voucher & receipt** Digital proof you claimed a drop or redeemed credit. Shops can reward people who hold them.

S.03 · How it works

## From launch to latte.

One shop, one customer, start to finish. Screens marked Real screen are the Swop app today; the others illustrate the step.

01 · Launch

### Your own currency, in minutes.

In the app, choose **Geo Bucks** (not a community token), give it a name and symbol, and set the lifetime ceiling: the most that can ever exist. One Buck is worth one dollar of credit at your stores, only you can issue more, and Swop covers the network fee.

02 · Issue

### Reward people by name.

You sign a claim, the customer collects it into their Swop wallet. No plastic cards, no points app, no spreadsheet.

03 · Drop

### Put rewards on the map.

Drops are rewards tied to a place. They appear on the map for people nearby, who claim them with an NFC tap, a rotating QR code, GPS or a beacon, and get a digital voucher. This is the real map: when nothing's nearby, it tells you.

04 · Spend

### Spent once. Gone for good.

Bucks are burned at checkout, so they can't be spent twice. The customer keeps a digital receipt that also works as proof of loyalty.

S.04 · Why it works

## Loyalty, without the software bill.

Store credit, rewards and receipts in one place, owned by the shop that issues them.

### One Buck, one dollar

Each shop's Bucks are worth $1 of credit at that shop's registered stores. Simple enough to explain at the till.

1 = $1

### Burned when spent

No double spending, no expired-points mess.

Issued → Held → Burned

### Your money, your keys

Each shop launches its own Bucks on Base. Swop can't create more of them.

“Swop holds no key that can mint a merchant's money.”

### Receipts that count

Every redemption leaves a digital receipt. Shops can reward the regulars who hold them.

Ember Coffee Visit 11

### Four ways to claim a drop

Pick the one that fits your counter, your street or your event.

**NFC tap** Tap a Swop card or sticker at the counter.

**Rotating QR** A code that changes, so screenshots don't work.

**GPS** Claim within a radius. Promo tier.

**Beacon** A small device that knows you're inside.

### AI can read it

Ask Claude or ChatGPT what credit you hold, through the Swop MCP.

Which Bucks do I have? 12 Ember Bucks and 3 Juniper Bucks.

Credit from every place you love sits next to your money, under your swop.id.

S.09 · Questions

## Asked and answered.

### What is a Geo Buck?

Store credit that a shop issues itself. Each Buck is worth $1 of credit at that shop's registered stores, and it sits in your Swop wallet next to your other money.

### Can I cash Bucks out?

No. Bucks are not redeemable for cash and are not guaranteed by Swop. Only the shop that issued them honours them, at its own stores.

### Who controls how many Bucks exist?

The shop. Each shop launches its own Bucks on Base and is the only one who can issue more. Swop holds no key that can mint a merchant's money.

### What happens when I spend them?

They're burned at checkout, so they can't be used twice. You keep a digital receipt, which the shop can use to reward regulars.

### How do I claim a drop?

Open the map in the Swop app, go to the drop, and claim it the way the shop chose: an NFC tap, a rotating QR code, being within range (GPS), or a beacon in the store. You get a digital voucher in your wallet.

Swaps, perps and prediction markets in one wallet, with a feed that shows what people actually trade. **Copy a trade in one tap.**

Feed cards: illustration · Phone: the real Swop app

Real screen · example data

Three things to know

## Trading on Swop, in three lines.

### One wallet, three markets.

Swap tokens, open perps and trade prediction markets without leaving the wallet you already use.

Live swaps · perps · predictions

### Markets are social.

Trades post to your feed. Copy a trader and the trade runs in your own wallet; they earn half the swap fee as SWOP.

0.5% swap fee · reward paid in SWOP

### Leverage is risk.

Perps can be liquidated and you can lose what you put in. Swop never promises returns.

How liquidation works →

S.02 · In 30 seconds

## Trading on Swop, explained simply.

If you can send a payment in an app, you can make a trade on Swop. Here's the whole thing in one screen.

What it is

One wallet where you can swap tokens, open perps and trade prediction markets, with a feed that shows what people you follow are doing.

Who it's for

People who already trade, and people who want to start small by following and copying traders they trust.

What it costs

0.5% on swaps. No Swop fee on perps or prediction markets today. Network or venue costs may apply, and you see them before you confirm.

What you need

A swop.id and some funds in your Swop wallet. Prediction markets aren't available in every country.

STEP 01

#### Open your wallet

Your swop.id comes with a wallet. Your tokens, perps and predictions all show up here.

STEP 02

#### Find a market

Browse top movers and trending questions, or search for any token.

STEP 03

#### Review, then confirm

You see the size, the fees and your safety settings before anything happens.

**Swap** Trading one token for another, like dollars-on-chain (USDC) for SOL.

**Perps** Short for perpetual futures: a bet on a price going up (long) or down (short), with no expiry date.

**Leverage** Borrowing to make a position bigger. 5× turns $100 into a $500 position, and makes losses 5× bigger too.

**Liquidation** If the price moves far enough against a leveraged position, it closes automatically and you lose the money you put in.

**Stop loss** An automatic exit you set in advance, so a position closes before it loses more than you're willing to.

**Prediction market** A market on a yes-or-no question. A price of 62¢ means people think the "yes" is about 62% likely.

S.03 · How it works

## Four markets. One wallet.

These are the real screens in the Swop app today (the wallet and swap show example numbers). Scroll to walk through each one.

01 · Swap

### Any token, any chain.

Pick what you pay with and what you want. Swop finds the best route across Solana, Ethereum, Base, Polygon, Arbitrum, Optimism and Robinhood Chain, including tokenized stocks. Use **Market**to trade now or**Limit** to wait for your price.

02 · Perps

### Perps, stocks included.

Go long (you think the price rises) or short (you think it falls) on crypto and stocks like NVDA, through Hyperliquid. Choose leverage, then set a take profit or a trailing stop that follows the price and only moves in your favour. No Swop fee on perps today.

03 · Predict

### Trade what happens next.

Pick a game or a question and buy the outcome you believe in. Prices work like odds: 62¢ means about a 62% chance. Markets run through Polymarket where it's allowed, and your positions come straight from there.

04 · Copy

### See it. Copy it.

The feed is where people share trades and ideas. When a trade is shared as a card, tap Copy and it runs in your own wallet at the size you choose. The trader you copied earns half of the swap fee as a SWOP reward.

S.06 · Leverage, honestly

## Bigger trades, bigger swings.

Leverage lets a small amount control a bigger position. It works the same way in both directions, so here is what it really means with $100.

No leverage (1×) **can't be liquidated**

2× · $200 position **~ -50%**

5× · $500 position **~ -20%**

10× · $1,000 position **~ -10%**

25× · $2,500 position **~ -4%**

Roughly how far the price can move against you before the position is liquidated and the $100 is gone (venue fees and funding move these numbers a little). The app shows your exact **estimated liquidation price** before you confirm, and a stop loss lets you leave earlier on your own terms. You can lose what you put in; you can't lose more than that margin on an isolated position.

Real screen

S.10 · Questions

## Asked and answered.

### What can I trade on Swop?

Token swaps on 7 chains (including tokenized stocks and real-world assets), perps on crypto and stocks through Hyperliquid, and prediction markets through Polymarket where they're allowed.

### What does it cost?

Swaps carry a 0.5% Swop fee. Perps and prediction markets carry no Swop fee today. Network and venue costs may still apply, and you'll see the details before you confirm.

### How does copy trading work?

When someone shares a trade, it appears as a card on the feed. Tap Copy and the same trade runs in your own wallet at the size you pick. The trader you copied earns half of the swap fee, paid in SWOP.

### Why can't I see prediction markets?

Prediction markets aren't available in every location. If they're restricted where you are, they won't show up.

### What is liquidation, and can I avoid it?

With leverage, a position closes automatically if the price moves far enough against you, and the money you put up for it is lost. Lower leverage gives the price more room, a stop loss closes the trade earlier on your terms, and the app shows the estimated liquidation price before you confirm.

### Will I make money?

We don't promise returns, and neither do the traders you follow or Ovi. Prices move against you as often as for you, and leverage makes losses bigger. Only trade what you can afford to lose.

In 30 seconds

## Live video, with a checkout.

Swop Live is live video inside the Swop app. You stream from your phone or browser, and the people watching can buy what you're showing without leaving the stream.

What it is

Live streaming built into your Swop profile, with your store one tap away for viewers.

Who it's for

Creators, shops and anyone who sells on camera. Teams and coaches who stream games get a pro camera app later.

What it costs

Going live is free. Sales use normal Swop checkout: a 0.5% fee (minimum 0.015 USDC) that the seller pays. Free accounts keep replays for 30 days, as the setup screen says.

What you need

The Swop app or a browser, and a swop.id. To sell, a product in your Swop store. Streaming software like OBS is optional.

How it works

Real app screen

STEP 01

#### Set up and go live

Name the stream, choose screen + camera or camera only, then go live. Already use OBS? Connect it as streaming software.

STEP 02

#### Pin it, sell it

Pin a product from your store. Viewers tap Buy and pay by card or crypto through Swop checkout, mid-stream.

STEP 03

#### Replay and restream

Your stream is saved as a replay. Restreaming (through Restream.io) sends the same video on to YouTube or Twitch at the same time.

**RTMP** The standard way streaming software such as OBS sends video to a server. Swop accepts it, so pro setups work.

**Restream** Sending one live video to several places at once. Swop sends it to your Restream.io account, which passes it on to YouTube, Twitch and others.

**Replay** The recording of your stream, saved after you end it so people can watch later.

**Pinned product** An item you put on screen during the stream; viewers tap it to buy without leaving.

S.08 · Questions

## Asked and answered.

### What can I stream from?

The Swop app on your phone, a browser, or streaming software like OBS over RTMP.

### Can I stream to YouTube and Twitch at the same time?

Yes, through Restream.io: connect your Restream account and Swop Live sends your broadcast there, which passes it on to YouTube, Twitch and others while you're live on Swop.

### Are my streams saved?

Streams are recorded as replays. If your connection drops and you reconnect, the pieces are stitched back together, and you can download the replay as an MP4.

### How do viewers buy, and what does it cost me?

Pin a product and viewers pay through Swop checkout by card or crypto. Buyers pay the list price; you receive USDC on the buyer's chain minus a 0.5% fee (minimum $0.015) that the seller absorbs.

### What is Streamy?

A pro producer app for iPhone and iPad with multiple cameras and a sports scoreboard overlay. It's still being built; when it's ready it will feed Swop Live.

S.07 · Questions

## Asked and answered.

### What is SWOP?

SWOP is an SPL token on Solana with a fixed supply of one billion. Inside Swop it pays for AI, rewards activity like copied trades and referrals, and is the currency of El Dorado.

### Does holding SWOP earn a yield?

No. Swop doesn't promise any yield or return for holding SWOP, and there's no staking product today. Planned Swop Chain roles (like a creator verification stake) are about access and security, never a payout.

### How do copy-trade rewards work?

When someone copies your trade, you, the trader they copied, get 50% of that swap's fee back as a SWOP reward. The copy runs in the follower's own wallet.

### How do referral rewards work?

For 12 months after someone joins with your invite, you get 50% of their swap fees, paid in SWOP.

### What is planned for SWOP?

On Swop Chain, which isn't built yet: a stake creators can put behind their name, a bond for AI agents, gas fees, and staking for the chain's operators. Until it ships, it's a plan, not a feature.

S.09 · Questions

## Asked and answered.

### Is Ovi available now?

Ovi is in beta inside the Swop app as your AI trading agent, and you can talk to it from Claude, ChatGPT or Grok through the Swop MCP. The standalone Ovi app for web, Mac and iPhone is still being built.

### Can Ovi spend my money without asking?

Anything that moves money shows you the details and waits for your approval. On top of that, per-payment and daily caps apply, and you can switch AI spending off at any time in Settings → AI assistants.

### Will Ovi make me money trading?

We don't promise returns, and Ovi doesn't either. It proposes positions inside the loss cap you set; markets can go against you.

### What does it cost?

AI usage is paid in Swop Credits, funded with SWOP. Ovi shows an estimate before each message, and your credit balance shows at the top of the chat.

### Does Ovi learn from my chats?

No automatic learning from your chats. If Ovi trains its own models, it will only use examples people have separately agreed to share, and that consent is separate from keeping your chat history.

Get started

S.02 · In 30 seconds

## The Swop MCP, in 30 seconds.

Paste one web address into ChatGPT, Claude or Grok, and that assistant can look people up, sell for you and, if you allow it, pay inside your limits.

What it is

A **connector**(a plug-in that lets an AI assistant use another app) that gives your AI 51 Swop tools. It speaks**MCP** (Model Context Protocol, the open standard assistants use to call outside tools).

Who it's for

People who already work in ChatGPT, Claude or Grok and want Swop there too, and developers building their own agents.

What it costs

Nothing to connect. Anything you buy, sell or swap costs the same as it does in the Swop app.

What you need

Nothing to look things up. For your own account you sign in with **OAuth**(you approve the link in the Swop app; no password goes into the chat), and spending stays inside your**caps** (per-payment and daily limits you set).

In the Swop app today · example data

In the Swop app, Settings → AI assistants shows the connector URL with a copy button, plus the switch for AI spending.

S.10 · Questions

## Asked and answered.

### What is MCP?

The Model Context Protocol is an open standard that lets AI assistants use outside tools, a bit like USB for AI apps. Swop runs a remote MCP server, so assistants that support custom connectors can use Swop directly.

### Which assistants work today?

ChatGPT, Claude and Grok, by adding https://mcp.swopme.co/mcp as a custom connector. A one-click Swop plugin in ChatGPT's directory is in review.

### Can my AI spend money without me?

Only if you turn AI spending on, and only inside the per-payment and daily caps you set. You can allow perps and swaps separately, and switch everything off or disconnect an assistant any time.

### Do I give my password to the AI?

No. The assistant opens a Swop sign-in page (OAuth 2.1), and approving it in the Swop app finishes the link. Nothing secret is typed into the chat.

### Do I need an account to try it?

No. Looking up swop.ids, searching people, browsing stores and reading prediction markets work with no sign-in.

Get started

Copy the URL, add it as a custom connector, and ask your assistant to look someone up.

[Full setup guide](https://mcp.swopme.co) [Set your caps](https://swopme.app/ai-assistants)

S.02 · El Dorado in 30 seconds

Three things to know

## Decentrabet, in three lines.

### You set the odds.

Anyone writes a question, picks fixed odds and a stake limit, and deploys their own market contract.

Beta testnet

### The contract holds the money.

Stakes sit in the market contract, not a Swop wallet. The validators you name resolve it, and Swop never runs the book.

Majority vote · contract pays out

### Testnet only, for now.

Base Sepolia with test USDC, contracts not yet audited, no real money. Legal review and geo-gating come before any real money.

[Try the testnet beta](https://decentrabet.vercel.app)

S.02 · Decentrabet in 30 seconds

Decentrabet lets anyone **create a yes-or-no market**on a question, choose the payout odds themselves, and let people they trust decide the result. Today it runs only with**free test money**.

Who it's for

**Creators and communities**who want to run their own markets instead of using someone else's book, and**developers** exploring on-chain markets and AI agents that play poker.

What it costs

**Nothing during the beta.** It runs on a testnet with test USDC, which has no value. Swop takes no fee, and there is no real money in it.

What you need

A crypto wallet that connects with **WalletConnect**, and some free test USDC on Base Sepolia. Signing in with your**swop.id** comes later.

Live site

STEP 01

#### Connect a wallet

Your wallet is your account. There's no email sign-up and Decentrabet never holds your keys.

Live site

STEP 02

#### Set the odds and deploy

Write the question, lock the odds and put up your own side. The market goes live as a contract you own.

Live site

STEP 03

#### Share it, then settle

Post the live card anywhere. When it closes, the validators you named vote, and the contract pays out by itself.

**Testnet** A practice copy of a blockchain. Its tokens are free and worth nothing, so mistakes cost nothing.

**Smart contract** A small program on a blockchain that holds money and follows fixed rules. Here, each market is its own contract.

**Validator** A person the creator names to judge the result. A majority of them decides the outcome.

**Audit** A security review of a contract's code by outside experts. Decentrabet's contracts haven't had one yet.

**swop.id** A Swop username like maya.swop.id. The plan is to show these on bets and use them to sign in.

**SmartSite** Your Swop page. A Decentrabet card can sit on it and update itself.

S.03 · How it works

## From a question to a settled market.

Here is one market, “Will it rain in Austin this Saturday?”, from the moment it’s created to the moment it pays out.

01 · Ask

### Ask anything. Set the odds.

Fixed odds, a stake limit, a closing time and the people who will judge the outcome. You choose all of it.

02 · Deploy

### It's your contract, not ours.

Each market is its own contract. Stakes sit in that contract, not in a Swop wallet and not with Decentrabet.

03 · Share

### Embed it anywhere.

A live card that updates itself, from open to settled. Drop it on your SmartSite, share it to the Swop feed, or paste it into any site.

04 · Resolve

### Named validators decide.

The people you named vote on the outcome. A majority resolves it, and the contract pays out on its own.

S.04 · The rules

## Simple math. Clear custody.

The short version: you pick the odds, the contract holds the money, and nobody at Swop or Decentrabet can take it.

### You set the odds

Fixed odds, a matched book, refunds on overage. The market math has 255 tests behind it.

2.4× you pick the number

### The contract holds the stakes

Not Swop, not Decentrabet. Swop provides identity and distribution and never runs the book.

Your stake → Market contract → Payout

### Poker on the same contracts

Tables use mental poker: a 2,048-bit encrypted deck and a signed relay, with no trusted dealer. An MCP server lets AI agents take a seat.

A K??

### For AI agents

25 poker tools through MCP.

25

**255** tests on the market math

**4** contracts: markets and poker tables

**25** MCP tools so AI agents can play poker

**2,048-bit** encrypted poker deck

**$0** real money: testnet only

S.05 · Honest status

## Where it stands, and the swop.id path.

Decentrabet was spun out of Swop in July 2026 so that creators own their markets. The plan brings it back as the first dApp you sign into with swop.id.

Testnet beta

- **Create and deploy markets** on Base Sepolia with test USDC.
- **Live embed cards** that track open, awaiting validators, resolved and settled.
- **Share to the Swop feed** as a live market post.
- **Poker relay and MCP server** for AI agents (browser seats are off for now).

Before real money

- **Legal review and geo-gating**, so markets only run where the law allows.
- **A contract audit** of the market and poker contracts.
- **Swivy in production** for Sign in with Swop.

The swop.id path

- **Phase 1 · names** (planned): bets, odds and validators show swop.ids instead of 0x addresses.
- **Phase 2 · Sign in with Swop** (planned): the same wallet you use in Swop, with a passkey and a cap you set per app.
- **Phase 3 · one ecosystem** (vision): cards across Swop, a building in El Dorado, agents reading markets within your caps.

S.06 · Plugs into

## Swop brings the people.

Identity and distribution come from Swop. The stakes stay in your contract.

For developers

### swop.id is coming to Decentrabet.

Names first, then Sign in with Swop. You can build the same way today.

[docs.swopme.co/identity Resolve swop.ids Live Show names instead of 0x addresses, and look people up by their swop.id. Read the docs](https://docs.swopme.co/identity)  [docs.swopme.co/swivy/sign-in-with-swop Sign in with Swop Preview One login and the same wallet across apps. Not generally available yet. Read the preview](https://docs.swopme.co/swivy/sign-in-with-swop)

S.07 · Questions

## Straight answers.

### Is there real money in Decentrabet?

No. It runs on the Base Sepolia testnet with test USDC, which has no value. Real money would need a legal review, geo-gating and a contract audit first, and none of that is done yet.

### Who holds the stakes?

The market's own contract. Not Swop, and not Decentrabet. Each market is deployed by the person who created it.

### Who decides the outcome?

The validators the creator named when setting up the market. A majority of them resolves it, and the contract settles on that result.

### Can I sign in with my swop.id?

Not yet. Today you connect a wallet with WalletConnect. Showing swop.ids on bets is the first planned step, and Sign in with Swop comes once Swivy is in production. WalletConnect will stay as an option.

### Is Decentrabet part of Swop?

It was spun out of Swop in July 2026 so creators own their markets and Decentrabet ships the tooling. It's coming back into the ecosystem as a dApp that uses swop.id, while Swop never runs the book.

### Can AI agents play?

Agents can sit at poker tables through Decentrabet's MCP server today, on testnet. Agents betting on markets would only happen inside caps a person sets, and only after the legal review.

**Testnet only**

Decentrabet uses test tokens on Base Sepolia. Contracts are unaudited. Nothing here is an offer of real-money betting.

Try it

## Ask a question. Set the odds.

Deploy your first market on testnet. It costs nothing but test tokens.

S.01 · Swivy by Swop Building

# Wallets and login, for every app.

Swivy is Swop's own wallet and identity platform. Your users sign in with an email or a passkey and **get EVM and Solana wallets on the spot**, with no seed phrase.

[Request early access](mailto:support@swopme.co?subject=Swivy%20early%20access) Sign in with Swop, explained [Developer console (preview)](https://console-staging.5-161-244-56.sslip.io/)

Email + passkey login EVM + Solana Agent permissions OIDC

Three things to know

## Swivy, in three lines.

### Wallets, login and signing.

Everything an app needs to give people a wallet, the way Privy does it, built and run by Swop.

EVM and Solana · web, React, Expo, Node

### One swop.id, every app.

With Sign in with Swop, people bring the same name and the same wallet to each app that adds the button.

El Dorado, Chalk and Decentrabet planned first

### Building, in staging.

Not in production yet, and Swop itself still runs on Privy today. Developers can ask for early access.

Building [Request access](mailto:support@swopme.co?subject=Swivy%20early%20access)

In 30 seconds

## Sign-in and wallets, done for you.

Every app that touches crypto needs two hard things: a way for people to sign in, and a safe place for their wallet keys. Swivy is Swop's service that does both, so an app doesn't have to build them itself.

What it is

A wallet-as-a-service: login, wallets and signing for other apps, built by Swop. Status: building. It runs in staging only. Swop's own app still uses an outside provider (Privy) today; Swivy is built to replace it.

Who it's for

Developers building games, marketplaces, AI agents or any app whose users need a wallet. Later, Swop's own apps.

What it costs

Not available yet, so there's no price. Early access is by request.

What you need

An app and a developer on your team. You add an SDK for web, React, Expo or Node.

How it works

STEP 01

#### Add it to your app

Drop in the SDK and your app gets a sign-in screen and wallet tools.

STEP 02

#### Your user signs in

Email code or passkey, or one tap on Sign in with Swop. An EVM and a Solana wallet are created on the spot, no seed phrase.

STEP 03

#### Your app asks to sign

The rules you set are checked first (limits, allowed chains), then an isolated signer signs, and your server gets a webhook.

**Wallet-as-a-service** A company runs wallet sign-in and key storage for your app, so you don't build it yourself.

**OIDC** OpenID Connect, the standard behind “Sign in with Google”. Swivy uses it for “Sign in with Swop”.

**Passkey** A login stored on your phone or laptop and unlocked with Face ID or a fingerprint. Nothing to type or forget.

**Custody** Who holds the keys that control a wallet. Swivy has two modes: keys kept in an isolated signer, or split between the user's device and Swivy.

**Signer** The locked-down part of the system that holds keys and approves transactions. It runs separately from everything else.

**Webhook** A message Swivy sends to your server when something happens, like a transaction going through.

S.02 · How it works

## From hello to signed.

What happens behind the scenes, from the moment someone signs in to your app to the moment a transaction is signed. Screens below are illustrations of the developer console.

01 · Login

### Email code. Then a passkey.

Users sign in with an email code, with passkey, authenticator app or SMS as a second factor. No wallet popups, no extensions.

02 · Wallets

### Wallets appear at sign-up.

An EVM wallet and a Solana wallet are created the moment someone logs in. Keys live in an isolated signer or are split with the user's device.

03 · Sign

### Intents in, webhooks out.

Sign messages, EIP-712 data and transactions on EVM and Solana. Queue transaction intents, sponsor gas, and get a webhook when it lands.

04 · Agents

### Give AI a key, not the keys.

Delegated session grants let an AI agent or a backend worker act for a user, inside limits the user set, and stop when they say so.

S.03 · Sign in with Swop

## One swop.id. Every app.

Swivy is an OpenID Connect provider. An app adds a "Sign in with Swop" button, and people arrive with their name, avatar and, if they allow it, the same wallet they use in Swop.

01 · App **Tap "Sign in with Swop"**

The app sends people to Swop's hosted login.

`/.well-known/openid-configuration`

02 · Swop **Log in, then consent**

Passkey or email code, then a clear screen of what the app is asking for.

`scope: openid profile wallets.read`

03 · Token **Name, avatar, wallet**

The app gets a signed ID token it can check against Swop's public keys.

`JWKS · refresh tokens`

04 · Same wallet **Signing with consent**

Payments ask for a passkey step-up and stay inside a per-app limit the person sets.

`per-app policy`

Planned first El Dorado Chalk Game Film AI Decentrabet Your app

S.04 · The platform

## Everything a wallet app needs, in one place.

### Two ways to hold keys

Pick per app. Neither shows users a seed phrase.

`managed_tee`

Keys live in an isolated signer built for AWS Nitro Enclaves.

`split_custody`

Created in the browser. The device keeps one share; Swivy stores only encrypted data.

### Gas sponsorship

Pay your users' network fees from sponsor wallets, set per network.

### RPC routing per environment

Choose where each environment talks to the chain, including Swop's own RPC gateway.

Base Ethereum Arbitrum Optimism Polygon Solana

### SDKs and a CLI

Drop-in shapes for web and mobile, a policy engine, and an agent CLI for wallets, funding and signing.

`web``react``expo``node`

S.05 · Why build it

## Renting it today, owning it next.

Swop uses Privy today. Swivy is how Swop moves that layer in-house, and offers it to other apps.

#### Privy today

- Pricing that grows with every person who signs up
- The wallet and identity layer sits with a vendor
- Signing depends on a vendor's quotas and uptime

#### Swivy

- **Costs follow signing and storage,** not head count
- **Swop owns** the wallet and identity layer, and Sign in with Swop
- **The same SDK shape**, so moving an app over is a swap, not a rewrite

Ready to try it? Start with the [React quickstart](https://docs.swopme.co/swivy/react-quickstart) or [Sign in with Swop](https://docs.swopme.co/swivy/sign-in-with-swop).

**6** networks, EVM and Solana

**4** SDKs: web, React, Expo, Node

**2** custody modes

**0** seed phrases to write down

**1** swop.id for every app

S.06 · Honest status

## Built, not shipped yet.

Swivy runs in staging today. It is not in production, and the Swop app still uses Privy for login and wallets.

Building now

- **API, console, isolated signer and worker**, running in staging.
- **Login, wallets, signing, intents, webhooks** and gas sponsorship.
- **Sign in with Swop** (OIDC) and delegated grants for AI agents.
- **SDKs** for web, React, Expo and Node, plus the agent CLI.

Next

- **Production** on Swop's own infrastructure.
- **Swop moves over**: new users on Swivy, existing users migrate.
- **Public docs** and early-access projects.
- **Sign in with Swop** in El Dorado, Chalk, Game Film AI and Decentrabet.

Later

- **Outside security audits.**
- **Threshold signing** and device-first keys with recovery.
- **Signers in more regions.**

S.08 · Questions

## Asked and answered.

### Can I use Swivy today?

Not in production yet. Swivy runs in staging while we finish the production deploy. Invited preview partners can sign in to the [developer console (preview)](https://console-staging.5-161-244-56.sslip.io/); it's staging, so don't use it for real funds. Everyone else: request early access and we'll reach out when projects open.

### Does the Swop app use Swivy?

Not yet. Swop runs on Privy today. The plan is a dual stack: new users on Swivy first, then existing users migrate.

### Who holds the keys?

You choose per app. In managed mode keys live in an isolated signer built for AWS Nitro Enclaves. In split custody the user's device keeps one share and Swivy stores only encrypted data, so Swivy can't sign alone.

### Is it audited?

Not yet. Swivy has not had an outside security audit. That is on the list before it holds real users' funds.

### What is Sign in with Swop?

A standard OpenID Connect login. Apps get a person's swop.id name and avatar, and with permission their wallet addresses, without building auth themselves.

For developers [Swivy docs](https://docs.swopme.co/swivy) [Sign in with Swop](https://docs.swopme.co/swivy/sign-in-with-swop) [React quickstart](https://docs.swopme.co/swivy/react-quickstart)

## The practical questions.

### Does the person tapping need the Swop app?

No. NFC reading is built into iOS and Android, and your page opens in their browser. The app is only for you, to edit what the card opens.

### Which phones can read it?

iPhone 7 and newer read it from the lock screen with no setup. Most Android phones from 2017 on read it the same way.

### Can I change where it points after I get it?

Yes, as often as you like. The card never changes: edit your Swop page and the card opens the new version.

### How do I pay?

By card through Stripe, or with USDC from any Solana wallet, right on this page. AI agents can pay in USDC on Base over x402.

### What about shipping and returns?

Shipping is shown on the product and added in your cart before you pay. For delivery questions or a return, email [support@swopme.co](mailto:support@swopme.co) with your order reference.

Three things to know

## The fee, in three lines.

### You pay it, not the buyer.

Buyers pay your list price. Swop's 0.5% comes out of what you receive, with a minimum of $0.015 a payment.

Live on every Swop checkout

### AI agents: 0% at launch.

When an AI agent buys from your link, you get the full price in USDC. No platform fee while agent payments launch.

[How agents pay](https://www.swopme.co/pay)

### Card is separate.

Verified sellers can take cards too; card payments show their own fee at checkout, so this calculator counts crypto and agent sales only.

[Crypto vs card](https://docs.swopme.co/payments/crypto-vs-card)

Questions

## The fine print, plainly.

### Who pays the 0.5%?

You do, the seller. Buyers always pay your list price; the fee comes out of what lands in your wallet, with a minimum of $0.015 a payment.

### Why does my average sale matter?

Fixed fees and minimums hit small sales hardest. A $0.30 fee on a $2 sale is 15%; Swop's minimum on a $2 sale is $0.015. The calculator uses your average sale to count how many payments that is.

### Is the 0% for AI agents permanent?

It's the launch rate for purchases made by AI agents. If it changes, we'll say so here and in the app before it applies.

### What about card payments?

Verified sellers can accept cards. Card payments show their own fee at checkout, so leave card volume out of this comparison.

### Where do these "today" numbers come from?

From you. We don't assume any processor's pricing: type in the percentage and fixed fee you pay now. The results are estimates, not a quote.

# Copy trading on Solana: how it works and where it goes wrong

Copying someone is a delegation, not a strategy. Your copy is a second, later, separate trade — and almost everything that disappoints people about copy trading flows from that one gap.

ST [Swop Team](https://www.swopme.co/blog/authors/swop-team) Nov 11, 2026 Updated Nov 11, 2026 8 min read Copy link [X](https://x.com/intent/tweet?text=Copy%20trading%20on%20Solana%3A%20how%20it%20works%20and%20where%20it%20goes%20wrong&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.swopme.co%2Fblog%2Fcopy-trading-solana) [Farcaster](https://warpcast.com/~/compose?text=Copy%20trading%20on%20Solana%3A%20how%20it%20works%20and%20where%20it%20goes%20wrong&embeds[]=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.swopme.co%2Fblog%2Fcopy-trading-solana)

Contents What copy trading actually is on Solana Three models, and who can move the money Five ways a mirrored trade loses money Why leaderboards select for luck The questions to ask before you copy anyone Where Swop fits FAQ

Copy trading is sold as a shortcut past having a strategy: find someone who is good at this, point your money at them, go back to your life. The mechanics underneath are less obliging. Nothing is actually copied. Software watches a wallet, notices it traded, and submits a different transaction from your account — later, at your size, at whatever price exists by then, with your costs. Two transactions, two prices, two outcomes. Before you evaluate a single leaderboard, it is worth being precise about that gap, because it is where the money goes.

Solana is where this pattern became ordinary, for a structural reason: every trade on a public chain is visible the moment it settles, so following a stranger’s trading needs no permission, no agreement and no cooperation from the stranger. That cuts both ways, and the second way is the one that rarely gets said out loud — unless a product runs a formal programme, the trader you are copying has not agreed to anything, owes you nothing, and may not know you exist.

## What copy trading actually is on Solana

Strip the branding and there are three moving parts. A **signal**: a wallet you have chosen to watch does something, and that something is public. A**rule**: how that signal becomes an instruction for your money — which tokens, what size, with what limits. And an**authority**: whatever lets a trade be signed on your behalf, or prompts you to sign it. Every copy-trading product is a particular set of answers to those three, and the answers vary far more than the marketing does.

Notice that the signal is the easy part and the only part the leaderboard describes. Public chain data tells you exactly what a wallet bought, when, and at what price. It does not tell you why, what the trade was hedging, how much of that person’s net worth was behind it, whether the wallet is one of several they run, or whether the position was opened as part of something that happens somewhere else entirely. A record of trades is not a record of a strategy. It is the footprints, not the walk.

The rule and the authority are where your outcome is actually decided, and they are usually described in a sentence, if at all.

The leaderboard is the last thing to look at. This is the first.

## Three models, and who can move the money

Products that let you follow someone else’s trading come in three shapes. They are not degrees of the same thing — they fail in genuinely different ways.

- **You deposit, they trade.** Your money sits in an account, vault or program balance that someone else operates. This is the simplest to build and the one where a bad outcome can be total, because the failure does not have to be a bad trade. The question that settles it is not whether withdrawals are allowed but whether withdrawing is an action you take or a request you make. If there is any circumstance in which you ask and wait, you are a creditor of whoever runs it, in addition to being exposed to their trading.
- **You keep custody, you grant a permission.** The funds stay at your own address and you approve a scoped on-chain permission that lets a program trade them. Nobody can send your tokens to themselves, which removes the worst case — but “non-custodial” is doing a lot of work in that sentence, and the scope is the entire safety story. What instructions can it sign? Over which tokens? Up to what size? For how long? And can you end it in one action, by yourself? A permission with no size bound and no expiry is not much narrower than custody.
- **It proposes, you sign.** Software spots the trade and asks you to approve a matching one. This is the safest arrangement available and it is honest about the trade-off: you cannot be both the sole signer of every transaction and faster than a bot. Each approval is a round trip through a human, and the gap between the leader’s fill and yours widens accordingly. It also quietly defeats the thing copy trading is marketed on, which is being asleep.

Pick which of those you actually want, then be suspicious of any product that claims the control of the third with the responsiveness of the second. Authority and speed trade against each other, always, and a design that appears to escape the trade-off has usually just moved the authority somewhere you did not read.

## Five ways a mirrored trade loses money

The disappointing case is not the one where the trader you followed was wrong. It is the one where they were right and you still lost, which happens often enough to be the normal experience rather than an unlucky one. Five mechanisms, roughly in order of how much they cost:

- **You buy their impact.** On a token without deep liquidity, a sizeable buy is part of why the price went up. The signal you are following is generated by the very order that moved the market, and your order arrives afterwards. The thinner the token, the bigger that difference — which means it is largest in exactly the trades that look most exciting on a leaderboard.
- **Predictable flow gets picked off.** A trade on a public chain is visible immediately, and so is the wave of copies that reliably follows a popular wallet. Being a known buyer, in a known direction, a known moment later is a weak position to bid from. The cost arrives as a worse price rather than as a fee, which is why people rarely notice it and almost never attribute it correctly.
- **Size is not risk.** Mirroring an amount is not mirroring a bet. Someone putting two per cent of a large book into a position and you putting forty per cent of a small one into the same token are not doing the same thing, and being right about the token does not rescue you from being wrong about the size. Any product that copies a fixed amount, or a fraction that is not the trader’s own fraction, is handing you a different trade with the same name.
- **Exits mirror worse than entries.** An entry is one clean buy and easy to detect. Exits are frequently staged, partial, routed somewhere else, or expressed by an instrument the mirror does not watch — and a mirror that misses a partial exit leaves you holding a position the trader you copied has already reduced. Most of the result in trading is decided by exits, and most of the reliability in copying lives in entries. That asymmetry is not a bug anyone is in a hurry to fix.
- **Costs accrue per mirrored trade, not per good one.** Every copy is a transaction with its own spread, its own slippage and its own network fee. A trader doing forty round trips a week generates eighty of yours, and the round trips that net to nothing for them are not free for you. Activity is the cost base; only some of it is the strategy.

And the trader can change The wallet that earned a record is not under contract to keep doing the thing that earned it. It can start chasing an incentive programme, test something new, run a second strategy from the same address, or begin selling into the flow that follows it. Nothing notifies you, and the leaderboard will keep showing yesterday’s record for a while.

## Why leaderboards select for luck

Sort a large number of wallets by return over a short window and the top of that list is mostly noise. This is not cynicism about traders, it is arithmetic: return over weeks is maximised by concentration and leverage, which is another way of saying it is maximised by variance. The wallets that took the biggest swings fill both ends of the distribution. You are shown one end.

What the ranking hides is everyone who is no longer in it. Take ten thousand wallets trading volatile tokens, rank them after a month, and the leaders will look extraordinary whether or not a single one of them has an edge — because the ones who swung just as hard and lost have dropped off the page rather than appearing next to them with a warning. A leaderboard is a list of survivors presented as a list of experts.

The filters that carry information are the dull ones, and they are usually available if you are willing to click past the headline figure. How long is the record, and does it include a month the market was unkind? How deep was the worst drawdown, and did the person keep trading the same way through it? How many trades is the result built on — a dozen is a coin flip with a chart attached. Did the return come from one token that worked, or from something that happened repeatedly? Is the record on-chain and reproducible by you, or is it a figure inside an app and a screenshot?

Then ask the question almost nobody asks: who pays this trader, and for what? If the answer is a share of the volume their followers generate, you have hired someone whose income rises with activity and is indifferent to your net result. That is not an accusation of bad faith. It is a description of an incentive, and incentives are more predictable than people.

## The questions to ask before you copy anyone

Everything above compresses into a short list. It is worth answering all of it in writing, before any money moves, because every one of these questions is harder to think about during a drawdown.

- **Custody.** Can I move my funds right now, by myself, with nobody’s cooperation? If not, who is my counterparty and what happens to me if they fail?
- **Scope.** What exactly is the permission allowed to sign — which tokens, which actions, what maximum size, over what period? Say the limit out loud. If you cannot, you have not found it.
- **Revocation.** Which single action actually ends this, is it in my control alone, and do I know where it is before I need it? Turning a toggle off in an app is not necessarily the same as revoking an on-chain permission.
- **Sizing.** Is my position proportional to my account or a fixed number? What does it do when a mirrored trade is larger than I can afford?
- **Exits.** Does it mirror partial exits and stop-outs with the same reliability as entries? If the answer is vague, assume it does not.
- **The record.** Long enough to include a bad month, deep enough in trade count to mean something, and verifiable on-chain rather than asserted.
- **The incentive.** Who pays the trader, who pays the platform, and on what basis.
- **Blast radius.** If this goes as badly as it reasonably can, at the worst possible moment, what fraction of my money was inside it? That fraction is the real position size, not the one in the interface.

A revoked permission is the only one you don’t have to trust Standing approvals outlive your interest in them. An arrangement you stopped thinking about six months ago can still be allowed to act, and the calm-day habit of reviewing what each of your wallets is approved to spend is worth more than any single decision about who to follow. The general version of that discipline is in our [wallet safety checklist](https://www.swopme.co/blog/ai-agent-wallet-safety-checklist).

## Where Swop fits

Swop runs on Solana, Ethereum, Base, and Polygon, and on the first question in this article it has only one answer available to it: You control your Swop wallet: nothing moves without your approval, you can export your private key, and Swop never holds your keys. Wallets run on Privy today. There is no account balance to be let out of, because there is no account balance. That is not a feature we can turn off for a particular product, and it is the reason the deposit model above is not something we can offer you even if it would be easier to build.

The same key property is what makes the exit from us boring, which is the part worth caring about: losing your phone doesn’t mean losing your funds — log in with your email on any phone and your Swop wallet comes back with it. You can also save your private key, which lets you open your assets in any wallet you choose. An app that holds your key is a place your money can be stuck. An app that doesn’t is a reader of the chain that you can walk away from.

Two smaller mechanics matter to anyone whose trades are being generated by something other than their own attention. Swop has a built-in swap: you get a quote and sign inside the app, without sending funds to an exchange or connecting to a separate site — so following a strategy does not require a trip to a venue that would hold your funds while you were there. And Swop routes Solana swaps through Jupiter and EVM swaps through LiFi, quoting Solana swaps with a 50 bps default slippage tolerance. That is a default rather than a ceiling, and it is adjustable, which matters here specifically: slippage tolerance is the setting that decides what a late fill is allowed to cost you, and a late fill is the defining feature of a copied trade.

On delegated authority, the thing we have actually built and written down is the AI agent, and it is worth describing precisely rather than by analogy. Swop’s agent proposes; you approve. Nothing signs without a tap, and the agent never holds keys — the third model above, by construction. Underneath it, Swop’s Goldman trading agent runs under an [ERC-8196-inspired policy layer](https://www.swopme.co/blog/erc-8196-agent-policy): each vault carries a versioned policy, expanding a policy’s authority requires the owner’s EIP-712 signature, and every enforcement decision is written to a per-vault hash-chained audit log. In other words, the scope question from the checklist has a written answer, widening the scope needs your signature rather than a setting, and the record of what was allowed is append-only.

Two honest limits on that, because a delegation page without them is marketing. Enforcement happens at Swop’s backend signing seam — the point every agent transaction must pass to be signed — and the audit chain makes any violation provable. It is not an on-chain guarantee. And the policy layer shipped Aug 28, 2026 and is running in shadow (observe-and-log) mode while it soaks; enforcement mode follows. Separately, and relevant to anyone deciding how much to trust any of this: Swop has not commissioned a third-party security audit to date. We would rather you knew that while you were reading the paragraph above than after.

Swop is on [iOS](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/swop-connecting-the-world/id1593201322), [Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.travisheron.swopapp), and the web at [swopme.app](https://swopme.app). For what any particular feature does today, [support.swop.id](https://support.swop.id) is the official channel — and it is the only one. Anyone who messages you first offering to trade on your behalf is not us.

## FAQ

### Is copy trading on Solana safe?

The trading is as risky as the trades. The part you can actually control is the arrangement around it, and that comes down to one question: who is able to move your money. If you deposit into an account someone else trades, withdrawing is a request you make to a counterparty. If the funds stay at your own address and you grant a scoped permission instead, nobody can send them anywhere else, and your exposure is whatever that permission allows. Read the permission before you read the leaderboard.

### Why did my copied trade lose money when the trader I copied made money?

Because you did not make their trade. You made a second, later, separate trade in the same token. You filled after them, often at a price their own buying helped create; your position was a different size relative to your account than theirs was to theirs; and the exit may have mirrored less reliably than the entry did. On a thin token those gaps are large enough to turn their gain into your loss without anything malfunctioning.

### Does copy trading mean giving someone my private key?

It should never mean that, and no legitimate product asks for it. A private key or recovery phrase is total, permanent control of everything at that address, and handing it over is not a delegation, it is a transfer. Real designs either custody funds you deposit, or ask you to approve a scoped on-chain permission, or ask you to sign each mirrored trade yourself. Anyone who needs your key or your seed phrase to copy trades for you is stealing from you.

### How do I pick someone to copy?

Not by sorting the leaderboard by return. A short window ranked by return puts the wallets that took the wildest swings at the top, and the ones that took equally wild swings and lost simply stop being shown to you. The filters worth using are the dull ones: how long the record is and whether it covers a bad month, how deep the worst drawdown went, how many trades it rests on, and whether the result came from one lucky token or from something repeated. Then ask who pays that trader and on what basis, because someone paid on the volume they generate has a reason to trade more than is good for you.

### Can I stop copy trading at any time?

That depends on the model, and it is worth knowing before you start rather than during a drawdown. Turning a feature off inside an app is not the same as revoking an on-chain permission, and a standing permission does not expire when you lose interest in it. Find out which action actually ends the arrangement, confirm you can take it without anyone else’s cooperation, and know where it is before you need it. Reviewing what every wallet of yours is approved to spend is a calm-day habit.
